home.mission: Mission: from the 42 piscine to artificial intelligence
home.name: Louis Cagnion
home.pitch: Tech & Data Engineering Apprentice at Groupe Tressol-Chabrier, trained at 42 Perpignan.

stops.title: First piscine
paragraphs: I humbly started coding during my first piscine at 42. Yes, I knew absolutely nothing about this world before starting the school's selection process. I did not even know what a terminal or an IDE was.

Someone told me about the school, their approach to learning programming, and the possible career paths after the core curriculum: it sounded interesting. So I tried the 42 piscine to see what I was capable of in this new environment.
As it turned out, I discovered a genuine passion during that selection process, even though starting from scratch was not easy.

One moment stood out in particular. At first, I was asking for help on the early exercises from people who already had programming experience. Then, when we moved on to C for most of the piscine, they were the ones coming to me for help because I had progressed further than them.

That was when I realised I might have potential in this field and, more importantly, that I genuinely loved practicing and improving. And yes, for those wondering, I helped them gladly. People had helped me get started, so it felt natural to give back.

Unfortunately, I did not pass my first piscine on the first try, even though my results were around the average of other candidates. I was disappointed, almost sad, but I went home with a new goal: try again and get into the school.

stops.title: Common core
paragraphs: We theoretically had three years ahead of us to complete the core curriculum. For my part, I wanted to throw myself fully into learning to code. I chose to challenge myself by completing every possible bonus on the projects I picked.
I also wanted to move quickly while maintaining quality work, because going fast without actually learning anything would have been pointless. That is what I tried to do throughout my studies.

Even if I was not as fast as some friends I met during my piscines who finished the curriculum in six months, I still managed to complete all core curriculum projects in a year and a half, with bonuses whenever possible.

stops.title: Tressol-Chabrier
paragraphs: I focus on projects I consider useful, either to advance toward my future programming goals, or because they can bring something valuable to others or to myself.

Once I completed my common core, I joined the Groupe Tressol-Chabrier headquarters in Montpellier as a full-time developer. There, I took part in the design of internal applications (data search, dashboards, admin back-office), working on both the frontend and backend, which let me put my skills into practice in real-world conditions.
You can find the projects I have worked on in the "My projects" section.

stops.title: RNCP 7 in AI
paragraphs: My underlying goal has not changed: once I complete this RNCP6, I plan to pursue a further one-year work-study program to earn an RNCP7 in AI and algorithmics. So I want to deepen my knowledge in the areas related to both qualifications, starting with software development, then AI and algorithmics for what comes next.

stops.title: AI research
paragraphs: In the longer term, my ambition is to contribute to AI research, with the goal of taking part in the advances toward artificial general intelligence (AGI), and beyond.
